title: Smart Hops: micro‑budget hedging + GPU‑class priority with progressive model fallback
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem: heavy tenant variance in spend and eviction risk causes noisy throttles and unpredictable latency. We need a routing policy that respects per-tenant short‑window budget caps, prefers cheaper spot capacity when safe, and gracefully degrades model variants (smaller/quantized) to avoid over‑spend without violating latency SLOs.

Proposal: Implement 'Smart Hops' router: a routing decision layer that executes a fast, probabilistic decision for each request using three inputs: recent spend velocity (sliding 5m and 1h windows), GPU class availability and eviction probability estimate for candidate regions, and per-tenant SLO weight. The router will: 1) allocate a tiny hedging buffer (micro‑budget slots) per tenant to allow short bursts on spot; 2) prefer GPU types based on cost per effective token (combines reported throughput and quantization capability); 3) escalate to a progressive fallback chain of model variants when projected spend breaches the cap or eviction probability exceeds threshold; 4) emit traceable routing reasons for observability and audits.
acceptance_criteria: Router makes deterministic choice for identical inputs in 99% of runs (minor randomization allowed for load distribution)
Per-tenant spend monitors enforce soft micro-budgets and move requests to fallback variants before hard cap is hit in 95% of simulated overload traces
Eviction avoidance: when region eviction probability > 0.25, route attempts to find on-demand or different GPU class with <=10% added latency percentile compared to baseline
End-to-end latency P95 for default path does not regress more than 5% after enabling Smart Hops
Rollback path exists: feature flag and per-tenant toggle; toggling off returns routing to current cost-router with zero config drift
Routing decisions include reason_code and diagnostics that show spend window, chosen GPU class, and fallback model id
updates: 2026-03-10: Initial ticket created by Aisha. Drafted high-level design and acceptance criteria.
2026-03-11: Technical review with Serving Runtime and Infra; asked to include eviction-prob estimator hook and fast cache for region scores.
2026-03-12: Added micro-budget slots concept; infra suggested shard-local budget counters and bloom-style prechecks to limit coordination overhead.

2026-03-13: Prototype plan accepted. Split work into router core (ENG task), eviction estimator (ML/infra), and model-fallback catalog mapping (model onboarding). Assigned owner for rollout and observability dashboards.
comments: Priya Patel (PM): Please ensure we surface clear billing signals to customers when fallback is triggered — they should be able to correlate degraded model variants with cost events.
Ravi Singh (Infra): We'll provide a region-eviction feed with 10s granularity. Suggest using exponential smoothing to avoid flip-flopping.
Kaori Nakamura (Runtime): Fallback to quantized variant must respect token-level cache compatibility; will add a KV-cache compatibility check in router decision path.

Markus Lee (Assignee): Plan to implement a lightweight scoring function first (cost_score + eviction_penalty + sLO_weight) and gate progressive fallback via a feature flag. Will deliver prototype end of cycle.
Security: No additional controls needed for routing metadata, but add audit log export for high‑spend tenant events.
implementation_notes: Routing decision will run inside gateway process (latency budget <=500us) — keep estimator calls local or via cached snapshot.
Micro-budget slots: allocate integer slots per tenant updated every 30s; slots replenish at a rate derived from tenant monthly commit and recent velocity.

GPU class ranking: calculate cost_per_effective_token = (instance_cost / observed_tokens_per_sec) * shrink_factor_for_quantization; prefer classes with lower value unless eviction penalty outweighs savings.

Progressive fallback chain example: full_model -> quantized_model_16bit -> distilled_model -> small_distilled_quantized. Each fallback should include expected latency delta and token-quality delta in catalog.
Fallback orchestration: pick variant that keeps projected spend delta within soft cap and predicted latency within tenant SLO multiplier.
Observability: emit metrics: routing.choice, reason_code, spend_window_rate, eviction_prob, chosen_gpu_class, chosen_model_variant. Add dashboard with heatmap of fallbacks by tenant and region.
testing_plan: Unit tests for score computation and micro-budget accounting
Integration test harness simulating region eviction spikes and verifying fallback timing
Chaos tests: force spot evictions and validate evasion and reroute correctness
Load tests to measure added latency and P95 impact with feature on
Canary rollout: 1% tenants -> 5% -> 20% with automated rollback on spend/regression signals
rollout_steps: Alpha: internal tenants only, feature flag default off (2 weeks)
Beta: opt-in for high-volume tenants with monitoring and billing notifications (4 weeks)
Gradual: enable soft caps for remaining tenants and monitor fallbacks and SLOs (4 weeks)
GA: default-on with tenant-level opt-out and SLA adjustments in contract negotiations
